definitions.meaning: a model is someone who poses, for an artist or a camera
a problem here is a puzzling question, a teaser

explanation.definitionFit: One who strikes attitudes for a painter is a sitter, and a tricky question is a puzzler: both are called by the same word.

parts.note: Vic is a short boy's name, the first of the pair
Tim is another short boy's name, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Someone is being bullied by a pair of lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One persecuted' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the whole definition; the two lads give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A target of cruel treatment is a sufferer, the usual sense of the word.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words anoint me could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be chosen and anointed, as for high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the eight letters of ANOINT ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a candidate is to pick them out for a post.

clue.text: The Case of the Burdened Traveller

definitions.text: The Case of the Burdened Traveller

parts.words: The Case of the Burdened Traveller
parts.note: reads like a detective story title, but the case is a suitcase and the burden is what a traveller carries

explanation.definitionFit: Suitcases and bags carried on a journey are a traveller's baggage.

clue.text: Mistake over part of book causes delay

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake
a page is part of a book

explanation.surface: An error over a section of a book holds up publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places SLIP above PAGE in the down light; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling behind schedule is called slippage in project management.

parts.note: fair hair is blonde
a trade is a skilled manual occupation

explanation.surface: A fair-haired person has a craftsman's job, as cover for smuggling.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair trade was an old euphemism for smuggling, long before it meant ethical buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, contraband dealing was jokingly dubbed honest commerce by those who practised it.

clue.text: Talking to oneself, that's in character

definitions.text: Talking to oneself, that's in character

parts.words: Talking to oneself, that's in character
parts.note: an actor speaking thoughts aloud alone on stage, in the role of a character in a play

explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic speech delivered alone, voicing a role's inner thoughts, as in Hamlet.

parts.note: not tucking a shirt in, but a folded tuck sewn into a garment

explanation.definitionFit: A fold sewn or pressed into fabric, as in a skirt, is a type of tuck.

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to die is to end

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether things get better when thousands perish.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair or put right something is to make it better.

parts.note: left means departed, got off
a wing is what gives flight; also a flight of a building

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist disembarks from a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialism sits on the political left, so a socialist is a radical of that side.

clue.text: Die where current flows back in river

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: flows back means the word for the current is read in reverse

parts.note: a rip is a strong sea current

explanation.surface: Someone drowns where a current runs back up a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flows back' turns RIP into PIR, which goes 'in' EXE, the Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass away is to breathe one's last, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Girl may seem mad, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A young woman might appear somewhat crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Girl may' as the definition, but 'may' is a link: the name is the girl, and the definition is just 'Girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a female first name, as in Jane Austen's novel.

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Greyhounds race round a cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic name for a burial ground by a church is the Lord's field.

definitions.meaning: in poker, a strong hand of three of a kind plus a pair
a theatre or venue with every seat taken

explanation.definitionFit: A poker hand of three plus a pair, and a sold-out venue with no empty seats, share the name.

definitions.meaning: a part of a town, like the Latin ...

explanation.definitionFit: One of four equal parts, and an area of a city, both bear this name.

clue.text: Regret failing to keep one's record book

indicators.note: to keep means the letters hold another piece within them
failing suggests the word regret goes wrong and falls into disorder

parts.note: one's read as one is, I'S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for not keeping their diary up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' is the anagram signal on Regret, and 'to keep' wraps it round the abbreviated 'one is'; the contraction one's must be read as one is.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ledger of names or events, such as a school roll, is a recorded list.

clue.text: Pieces of cotton hardest to unravel

indicators.note: unravelling undoes the order of the word hardest, letting it be rewoven

explanation.surface: Lengths of cotton that are the toughest to untangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of cotton yarn used for sewing are strands.

clue.text: Conceal problems within — one's not on the level, naturally

definitions.text: one's not on the level, naturally

indicators.note: within means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: to hide is to conceal
ills are troubles or problems

explanation.surface: Someone dishonest hides their troubles inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on the level' suggests dishonesty, but it means a natural slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope of the ground is literally not flat, and nature made it so.

parts.note: stuck means baffled, unable to proceed
up as in up in arms, in revolt

explanation.surface: Someone confused and mutinous comes across as haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbish and conceited people are said to hold their noses high.

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the yellow flag is a kind of iris
bombast is ranting, inflated talk

explanation.surface: Shameless pompous speech from someone called Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the two pieces beside each other; Iris looks like a woman's name but is the flower, a FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaring, brazen behaviour is done openly, without shame.

indicators.note: lost her first means the opening letter of the name is dropped

explanation.surface: Sally's first colleague left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost her first' drops S from SALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or associate who works alongside you is a friend on your side.

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Look, engineers are studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional knowledge passed down is a body of learning.

indicators.note: held in means one piece is gripped inside another

parts.note: red is a common word for a communist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A communist is kept in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: Red has long been slang for a communist, from the red flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in custody before trial is called being on remand.

clue.text: Weeps, about to rise in confusion

parts.note: C stands for circa, about

indicators.note: in confusion means the word rise is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sobs, ready to get up in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the Latin circa, abbreviated; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding tears is crying; sobs is a synonym.

parts.note: Samuel Morse invented the Morse code

explanation.surface: Samuel leaves behind a small snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small bite or mouthful.

parts.note: cash is ready money
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: A shop sells cloth for cash payments only.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft goat-wool cloth is a luxury textile.

clue.text: Request we rejected as out of line

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: rejected means the word we is sent back, so read backwards

explanation.surface: We turned down a request that was inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns WE into EW; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked or awry means not straight.

clue.text: Wonderful thing doctor's given to one in need of food

indicators.note: in means the joined pieces go inside

parts.note: hunger is the need for food

indicators.note: given to means one piece is joined to another

parts.note: MD is a doctor of medicine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor treats someone starving.
explanation.walkthrough: MD joined to I goes 'in' HUNGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an informal word for something outstanding, a corker.
